issues.what: Widened false 'INTERRUPTED' for completed run jobs, and the completed result is dropped. A row in 'triggering' with type='run' means the command ALREADY EXITED and _trigger was mid-delivery. bg_reset_stale_triggering() now flips it to 'active' at any age, so restore_from_db routes it to _interrupt_run_notify, which sends '[Background job INTERRUPTED] … Прерван рестартом сервиса, повторный запуск не выполнялся.' and fails the job. The headline is false (the job completed), the persisted tail in bg_jobs.last_output (written periodically by _run_exec via bg_update_output) is never attached to that body, and if session.send already logged the '[Background job completed] …' user_message before the crash the transcript now holds two contradictory messages for one job (logs.event_id is not UNIQUE, nothing dedups). Concrete cost: a finished codex_review verdict is discarded and the agent is told it never ran → re-runs a $0.13–0.24 round. Before the change this hit only rows >120s old (rare — _trigger normally takes seconds); now it is the norm for any run job caught mid-delivery, i.e. exactly what a restart produces. Evidence the path is live: production already holds 5 bg_jobs rows failed with that exact reason string. Cheap fix inside the author's own file: return the reset ids so restore_from_db can distinguish 'was delivering' from 'was executing' and attach last_output instead of asserting no re-run happened.

issues.where: app/db.py:_migrate — the `if 0 < max_price < 1000` branch and the marker INSERT after it
issues.what: The money mutation this fix is about still fires silently, with zero journal evidence. The author knowingly leaves one hole open (an existing DB with no marker whose MAX(tm_tasks.price_rub) is 1..999 gets one x1000 pass across tm_tasks, tm_payment_allocations, tm_payments, tm_clients on the first start after this change). Defensible — but the diff touched exactly these lines and added no logger call, so if it fires on some DB (the VPS copy, a restored backup, another project's DB) it is undetectable afterwards: no log line, and the marker written afterwards is identical in the fired and no-op cases. One `logger.warning("money units v1 migration fired: max_price=%s", max_price)` inside the branch, or storing max_price as the kv value instead of the constant '1', makes the residual hole observable for one line of code. I verified production is genuinely safe: max price_rub 50000, max paid_rub 29000, 763 tasks, marker absent → guard false → pure no-op.

The sender half of the P1 defect is not fixed — only the payload was enriched, and no consumer renders it. `send_message` returns rendered TEXT, not the receipt dict: `_message_delivery_receipt_text` (app/mcp_stdio.py:1244) special-cases only DELIVERY_UNKNOWN and FAILED_BEFORE_SUBMIT, so a QUEUED row behind a blocked head still prints verbatim `Message accepted to 'W'; delivery_id=...; state=QUEUED.` — literally the pre-fix symptom in the defect title. There is no machine-readable signal either: `_next_action` (app/message_deliveries.py:93) still returns `{}` for QUEUED, so `queue_blocked` is the only carrier and it is dropped on the floor. Only the polling tool `message_delivery_status` (which returns the raw dict) can see it, and nothing tells the sender to poll. The author disclosed this in risk note 1, but the 'changed' text claims 'every receipt path (accept, replay, GET) tells the sender the queue is blocked' — that is true of the JSON and false of what an agent reads. End-to-end the change is currently unobservable to any sender.

The new resolve endpoint has no operator gate, while the code it lives in declares the opposite invariant. The docstring says «Единственный писатель `resolution`: человек» and the comment at _TERMINAL_DELIVERY_STATES says «пишет ТОЛЬКО человек ... Автомат в это состояние не переводит никогда» — but `POST /api/message-deliveries/{id}/resolve` takes no `Request`, calls neither `require_operator_session` nor `require_operator_csrf`, and so is satisfied by the global cookie-OR-internal-token middleware. Every worker has INTERNAL_TOKEN in its worktree `.env` and a shell, so any agent can clear ANY delivery's barrier in ANY project and write an arbitrary `actor` string. The asymmetry is inside this one resource: the GET sibling 20 lines above (app/routes/sessions.py:1125-1167) explicitly 403s a cross-sender read (`row["source_session_id"] != source_id`), so a worker may not READ someone else's receipt but may REMOVE its barrier. The merge-resolve sibling cited as precedent guards a caller's own merge; this guards the #380 R7 anti-reordering barrier. Fix is the author's own one-liner: `require_operator_session`.

issues.where: app/harness/loop.py:106-109 (`run()` appends `user_entry` first) together with app/backend_harness.py:249-252 (leftovers now survive into the next turn)
issues.what: Carried-over steering is delivered in the wrong chronological position, unmarked. `run()` appends the NEW turn's user message first, then round 0 drains the leftovers, so a stale message ends up LAST — the strongest recency slot. Verified by direct probe in an isolated copy: with `_injected = ['STALE steering from the aborted turn']` and `send('NEW operator instruction')`, the history the model sees is exactly `['NEW operator instruction', 'STALE steering from the aborted turn']`. Concrete failure: another agent steers 'use endpoint X' while a turn runs, the operator interrupts and sends 'forget that, do Y instead' — the model reads 'do Y' then 'use endpoint X' and follows the stale one. Worse across a task boundary: after `switch_worker_branch` and a new task_id, steering written for the old task arrives attached to the new one with nothing saying so. Silent loss was worse, so the direction is right, but as written the fix trades silent loss for silent wrong-instruction-following. Closable inside the owned files: drain leftovers BEFORE appending `user_entry`, and/or prefix them ('[carried over from the previous turn] …') so the model can tell they are not the latest word.

NEW defect introduced by the fix: the branch prints ONE next step for a state that has TWO causes, and for one of them the instruction can never work. `app/message_deliveries._failure` produces either `DELIVERY_NOT_SUBMITTED` (quota, retryable: true) or `TARGET_TASK_CHANGED` (retryable: false). The new text ignores `error['retryable']` — which it already reads three lines above — and tells both: «once the cause is gone, resend the SAME text with the same delivery_id … a new id would create a second logical message». For TARGET_TASK_CHANGED that is a guaranteed loop: app/routes/sessions.py:786 re-accepts an existing row with `target_generation=existing['target_generation']` (the FROZEN value), and app/manager.py:1138-1148 re-compares that frozen string against the live session, so every resend with the same id raises TargetTaskChangedError again → FAILED_BEFORE_SUBMIT again. The cause is by construction not «gone» (that is exactly what the ABA guard frozen in tests/test_message_delivery_receipts_380.py:1419 asserts), and the only action that can deliver — a new delivery_id addressed to the target's current generation — is the one the new text explicitly warns against. Verified live: the formatter with code=TARGET_TASK_CHANGED emits the same «resend the SAME text with the same delivery_id» sentence. The old text was vague and wrong; the new one is confident and wrong, which is worse for an agent that follows it. Branch on the code (or on `error['retryable'] is False`) and say «this delivery id is dead, send a new message to the target's current task».

issues.where: app/mcp_stdio.py:648-668 `_delivery_receipt_text` (printed by `spawn_worker` at line 1060, three lines below the author's own edit)
issues.what: The identical defect the P1 fix was written for is still live at the sibling call site in the same file, on the same reconciliation flow the author was reasoning about. `_delivery_receipt_text` hardcodes «Task accepted.» and then appends the state, so a spawn whose POST timed out and whose reconciling GET found the row terminally refused prints: «Worker 'child' spawned. Model: opus. Task accepted. delivery_id=…; state=FAILED_BEFORE_SUBMIT.» Reachability confirmed by reading the path: `_post_initial_delivery` → `except ApiToolError` → `_reconcile_initial_delivery` (reconciles whenever outcome_unknown or status ≥ 500) → `_is_delivery_receipt` accepts ANY state → `return status` → spawn prints the receipt and does not raise. Output reproduced verbatim by calling the function. Consequence is worse than the message case: the orchestrator reads «spawned, task accepted», walks away, and the worker never receives its task — the same class of silent loss the P1 rationale cites. The P1 fix is correct but narrow; the pattern was not swept.

Confirmed red, exactly as disclosed: `1 failed`, with `'task': 'do it\n\n⚠️ ДРУГОЙ РЕПОЗИТОРИЙ…'` against the frozen `'task': 'do it'`. The diff as delivered leaves the tree failing a test mapped to app/mcp_stdio.py, so it blocks the merge gate until someone who owns that file edits it. Of the two repairs the author proposes only the first is safe: asserting the note is present keeps the oracle covering «delivered text == retry text». The second (setting the fixture to git_common_dir="/s/.git" so the note is empty) makes the oracle vacuous for exactly the behaviour this fix adds — a cross-repo spawn could again hand back a retry payload that differs from what was delivered and no test would notice. Do not take option two.

issues.where: app/session.py AgentSession.interrupt (grace block at ~2591-2607) vs app/backend_codex.py disconnect / _disconnect_scoped / _wait_scope_empty (CODEX_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=5)
issues.what: Worst-case interrupt() now exceeds the 30s HTTP timeout the author budgeted against, converting a false report into an ambiguous one. The stated budget "codex ack <=5s + 10s grace + disconnect" omits that CodexBackend.disconnect() itself opens with `if self._active_turn_id and proc and proc.returncode is None: await self.interrupt()` (another <=5s via wait_for(..., timeout=5)), and that on the scoped launch path `_disconnect_scoped` can burn `_wait_owned_process` 5s + `_wait_scope_empty` 5s -> TimeoutError -> KILL + 5s + 5s, i.e. up to ~20s more. Total ~5 + 10 + 5 + 20 = ~40s against the 30s default in `_api` (app/mcp_stdio.py). Because `_lifecycle_lock` is held for the whole window, the orchestrator's near-certain retry of stop_worker blocks on the lock and times out too. Per this project's own rule, `transport_timeout: ReadTimeout` on a mutating tool is the worst outcome class (state unknown, retry unsafe) — strictly worse than a report that merely lies. Suggested: drop INTERRUPT_TURN_END_GRACE to ~5s and/or wrap the escalation in asyncio.wait_for so the whole call is bounded well under 30s.

On the NON-scoped Codex launch the escalation kills the app-server but not the tool's children, so the worktree writes the defect is actually about can continue — the report stays false, just faster. `_connect_unlocked` falls back to a plain `create_subprocess_exec` when `_codex_scope_support()` fails (no user bus / no lingering), and that spawn passes no `start_new_session` and no process group. `_disconnect_direct` then does `proc.terminate()` / `proc.kill()` on the app-server pid alone, so a `pytest` (the author's own example) started by the in-flight tool call is orphaned and keeps writing. The scoped path is fine (`systemctl --user kill --kill-whom=all` empties the cgroup). The claim "with this fix the sentence they print is no longer false" is therefore conditional on launch mode and is not qualified anywhere in the notes or the code comment.

issues.where: app/backend_claude.py interrupt (~1130) vs app/session.py interrupt (per_turn guard at ~2598)
issues.what: The stop-honesty fix does not cover Claude workers, and the stated reason for excluding them is factually wrong. The rationale says Claude "already waits for the CLI's control response" — but ClaudeBackend.interrupt() returns True the moment the SDK control request is acknowledged inside CLAUDE_INTERRUPT_TIMEOUT; it does not wait for the turn to end. That is precisely the "the ack is the wrong signal" argument used to reject the Codex ack. The mechanical half of the exclusion (persistent stream, listen task never ends between turns, so `_listen_task.done()` is not a turn-end signal) is sound and I would not have changed it — but the consequence should be stated: the MCP sentence "Worker X interrupted and set to idle" remains potentially false for every Claude worker, which per CLAUDE.md routing is a large share of the fleet. The defect is fixed for codex/grok/harness only.

The claim "every other RUNNING->IDLE in the codebase publishes, so the three heartbeat paths were plainly the outliers" is false: `POST /api/sessions/{name}/restart-cli` is a fourth, unfixed site of the exact same pattern — `await session._disconnect_backend(); session.status = AgentStatus.IDLE; session._persist()` with no publish_turn_finished(), and the route does not refuse while RUNNING (unlike its neighbour clear-session, which does). The done-callback does not cover it either: `_disconnect_backend()` cancels `_listen_task`, and `_on_task_done` bails out at `except asyncio.CancelledError: return` before reaching its publish. Pre-fix this stranded a parked switch/merge forever; post-fix the 1s recheck bounds it to a second — so this is evidence FOR the second half of the fix and against the stated rationale for the first. File is outside the author's ownership, so it wants a report, not a silent edit.

The test covers only ONE of the three heartbeat publish sites it claims to fix. `session._last_msg_time = 0` (test line 46) makes heartbeat_loop's zombie block statically unreachable, because it is guarded by `if s.status == AgentStatus.RUNNING and s._last_msg_time > 0`. So the "dead process runtime" (session_hibernate.py:142) and "zombie with backend=None" (:160) branches are never entered; deleting either of those two new publish_turn_finished() calls leaves the suite green. Only the failed-reconnect branch (:190) is exercised. This is the "N red oracles on one seam" trap inverted: one test standing in for three sites.

`restart_preflight` now returns the constant `{"ok": True}`, and `restart_server`'s `if not verdict["ok"]: raise HTTPException(409, verdict["reason"])` is unreachable in production — kept alive only by tests/test_fd_adopt.py::test_t6_restart_endpoint_refuses_before_touching_systemd, which patches `restart_preflight` itself to return `{"ok": False}`. That is a test of a mock guarding code that exists for the mock. The author flagged it and correctly declined to touch a file he does not own; it should be one follow-up ticket removing the branch, the dict contract and both fd_adopt assertions together, otherwise the next reader treats the 409 path as live behaviour.

Dead code adjacent to the touched area, plus a stale claim resting on it: `_blocking_runtimes()` has zero callers anywhere in app/ (rg finds only its own definition), and `_DRAIN_DEADLINE_S` is 0.0. CLAUDE.md still describes `restart aborted (N non-adoptable turn(s) still running)` as a live defect delaying restarts up to 15 minutes; after this change nothing in the restart path can produce that outcome. Not introduced by this diff, but the diff is what makes the description false, so retire the note in the same pass.

issues.where: app/routes/system.py — the `"limit_pct": None if progress is None else line_limit(progress)` entry in the `buckets.append({...})` block
issues.what: Two owners of "the threshold" now exist and only the dead one has test coverage. `buckets[].limit_pct` in /api/usage/quota-map is still computed as the straight `line_limit(progress)` with no lane, is now read by no front-end code (grep for `limit_pct` in app/static/js finds only `lane.limit_pct`), and is still asserted by tests/test_quota_map_api.py:436,441. The next reader greps the payload, finds a tested field named `limit_pct` on the bucket, and reintroduces exactly the divergence this fix removed. Either drop the field or mark it reference-only where it is built.

The rewritten docstring says accumulated mutations are still given the drain budget ("Накопленным мутациям по-прежнему отдаётся весь бюджет"), but `MUTATING_DRAIN_BUDGET_S` is 0.0, so `drain_mutating_requests()` skips its loop entirely and awaits nothing. That docstring is now the only explanation of the function's behaviour and it overstates what the retained call does; someone restoring a non-zero budget later would silently restore a wait nobody asked for.

Контракт «токен одноразовый» СЛОМАН на стороне доставки, и охраняющий его тест теперь проходит вакуумно. Ветка `idx is None` не различает два разных случая: (а) «батч уехал без нас» (ради чего фикс и написан) и (б) «мы этот токен уже отрезолвили» — во втором `reservation` уже затёрт в `None`, `next(...)` не находит запись, и содержимое уезжает агенту ВТОРЫМ сообщением. Проверено прогоном, не заявлено: два подряд `_resolve_media(token, ...)` дают `_manager.send('sid-dup', '[23:00] SECOND')` при пустом ожидаемом. Существующий `test_media_token_is_single_use` при этом ЗЕЛЁНЫЙ (6 passed), потому что ассертит только `buf.entries`/`pending_media`, а не факт доставки — то есть страховка, заведённая ровно под «протухший токен ничего не делает», после правки не проверяет ничего. Сегодня из прода недостижимо (`handle_voice` и `handle_video_note` резолвят по одному разу на каждой ветке и делают `return`), поэтому не blocker, но дверь открыта беззвучно. Лечение: помечать reservation потреблённым (модульный `set()` или мутабельный флаг в токене — сейчас `_MediaToken` `frozen=True`) и уходить в позднюю ветку ТОЛЬКО по признаку «батч уехал», а не по «записи нет».

issues.where: app/tm.py — `_api_update_task_if_current_unlocked`, canonical (non-shadow) branch: `candidate = store.task_update_if_current(...)` … `legacy = _legacy_api_update_task_if_current(...)` … `return _canonical_result(...)`; plus `_canonical_result` and `_apply_finalization_task_update`. Callers: app/rout
issues.what: Legacy rejection after the canonical write is reported as SUCCESS. The author added a guard for `not candidate.get("ok")` but none for `not legacy.get("ok")`. `_canonical_result` returns `{**candidate, **_candidate_receipts(...), "projection_debt": debt}`, so `ok` comes from the candidate (True) even when legacy returned `{"ok": False, "error": "prevalidated task revision changed before status update"}`. The mismatch survives only inside `projection_debt.mismatches.ok`, which no caller reads. Because the finding-1 fix makes canonical acceptance unconditional (the revision is re-read from `detail` a few lines above), the legacy CAS is now the only staleness detector left — and its verdict is the one being discarded. Both callers in app/routes/sessions.py (switch_worker_branch at ~:2466, v1 merge path at ~:2288) branch on `result["task_status"].get("ok")` and therefore take the success path: canonical says in_progress + bound, while the legacy `tm_tasks` row is still `status='new', worker_session_id=NULL`. That is the state CLAUDE.md calls «невозможное состояние», which makes the merge gate refuse forever (`task 'N' is not bound to session '<id>'`). Window is wide, not theoretical: the identity is resolved at sessions.py ~:2347 and used at ~:2466, with a git branch switch plus lifecycle persistence in between (seconds), and any legacy-only writer bumps the revision inside it (bind_task_to_session, an agent's task_update, requeue/heir election). Pre-fix the same case raised `KeyError: 'stable_id'` → `task_assignment_raised` → branch rollback + quarantine: loud and recoverable. The fix trades a loud crash for a silent two-store divergence. `_apply_finalization_task_update` has the identical hole: in canonical mode `result.get("shadow_match")` is None, so its `replay_match`

issues.where: app/tm.py — `api_update_task` (IA wrapper, canonical branch after the `if context.mode == "shadow"` block); `link_commits_to_task` (IA wrapper, canonical branch).
issues.what: The finding-3 defect class is still live at two other call sites; the author fixed exactly one. `api_update_task` does `candidate = store.task_update(par, **candidate_args, expected_head=store.canonical_head)` and only THEN `legacy = _legacy_api_update_task(*legacy_args)` — with no try/except and no compensation at all. Every legacy-only validation the author cites as the reason to reorder `api_create_task` lives on that second call: `parse_acceptance_command`, `_normalize_acceptance_actor`, `_normalize_acceptance_manifest`, `raise ValueError("required acceptance oracle has no command")`, and `raise ValueError("Cannot change price on cancelled task")` inside `update_task`. `acceptance_actor` is not even in `candidate_args` because the store does not accept it — the same asymmetry cited for create. So one 400-worthy `task_update` mutates canonical, bumps the canonical revision, and leaves legacy untouched. That is strictly worse than the create case it mirrors: there is no `_discard_shadow_created_task` equivalent to undo a canonical update, and the resulting revision drift feeds straight back into the CAS problem of finding 1. `link_commits_to_task` has the same canonical-then-legacy shape. The author's own rationale is a statement about the module, not about one function, yet it was applied at one site.

issues.where: app/tm.py — `api_create_task` (IA wrapper), the new `try: candidate = store.task_create(...) except Exception: _discard_shadow_created_task(legacy); raise` block; compare against the `candidate_absent` probe in the `if context.mode == "shadow"` branch of the same function. Store side: app/ia/task_st
issues.what: The new compensation is a weaker copy of the shadow branch it claims to reuse, and its failure mode is the exact wedge this task was about. The new `except Exception:` calls `_discard_shadow_created_task(legacy)` unconditionally. The shadow branch does NOT: it first probes `store.task_get(str(legacy["par"]), project=legacy["project"])` and deletes the legacy row only when `candidate_absent` is proven (`str(probe_error) == f"{legacy['par']} not found"`), logging an ambiguous probe otherwise. That probe exists because a canonical create can fail AFTER it has written: `task_create` → `_commit_generation` writes the event JSON, then `_write_states` unlinks stale `state.json` files, writes every state file including the new task, and only then calls `_rebuild_projection` against a separate SQLite file under `~/.local/state`. A raise from `_rebuild_projection` (or anything after the state writes) leaves the canonical task fully materialised while the exception propagates. The new code then deletes the legacy row → canonical `_next_display_number` = n+1, legacy `_next_par` = n → permanent `task display counter mismatch`, i.e. the same project-killing wedge as finding 2, produced by the fix for finding 3. Second gap in the same block: the return value of `_discard_shadow_created_task` is discarded, whereas the shadow branch logs `"shadow task create compensation refused for %s#%s"`. Its WHERE clause requires `sync_revision=0 AND worker_session_id IS NULL AND git_commits='[]' AND NOT EXISTS(reservation)`, so refusal is possible and would silently leave legacy one ahead. Neither path is tested: `test_rejected_create_leaves_display_counters_aligned` fails on the legacy side, before the try block is entered, so the entire compensation is uncovered.

issues.where: app/workspace.py::merge_worktree_to_main — `except ValueError as e:` around resolve_base_branch
issues.what: Fix 2 is keyed on the exception TYPE instead of the POSITION in the flow, so the identical defect stays reachable from the same line. resolve_base_branch also raises RuntimeError (app/workspace.py::_inspect_branch_ref, when `git show-ref --verify` exits with anything but 0/1 — corrupt repo, permissions) and OSError (subprocess inside _git_cmd / _resolve_repo). Those still escape merge_worktree_to_main, hit the route catch-all in app/routes/sessions.py (`except Exception` -> state='partial', commit_point='unknown', HTTP 500) and hold the task reservation — exactly the defect being fixed. The author's own justification ("validating the target touches no ref, so the Git outcome is known: nothing happened") applies to them identically: the call is the first statement inside repo_mutation_lock, mutation_started is False, original_branch is None. Catching Exception there is as provably safe as catching ValueError.

issues.where: app/workspace.py::merge_worktree_to_main — the dict returned by the new except branch; consumed by app/merge_operations.py::normalize_merge_result
issues.what: The fix-2 early return drops fields every sibling refusal supplies. No `_http_status`: normalize_merge_result passes `status=raw.get("_http_status")` into the error envelope, so this path alone reports `"status": null` while every other pre-merge refusal built by _merge_not_reached carries 400/409. It also returns worker_branch="" and worker_head="", although the route already knows pinned_branch/pinned_head and reported them on the old escaping path — the failure report is slightly poorer than what it replaces. Classification itself is correct: "cannot resolve target branch: local base branch 'X' does not exist in …" reaches TARGET_MISSING in _classify_failure (no earlier rule matches), and normalize_merge_result yields FAILED / NOT_REACHED / git.status=FAILED, strictly better than the old UNKNOWN + blocking RECONCILE.
